title: The Complete Guide to Mental Health: Nutrient Recommendations and Lifestyle Advice
description: We are living in a Post-Covid world where stress levels have soared, challenging our mental resilience like never before. Juggling unprecedented demands on family, work, and personal health with conflicting information leaves many feeling overwhelmed and uncertain. Enter The Complete Guide to Mental Health: Nutrient Recommendations and Lifestyle Advice – your indispensable resource for navigating these tumultuous times. Authored by Dr. Carolyn Dean, an internationally known doctor who is an expert in nutritional therapies, this book delivers decades of expertise and tools tailored to bolster your mental well-being. Unlock the secrets to: Building Overall Health and Wellbeing: Cultivate a balanced life with proven strategies that nourish both mind and body. Supporting Your Brain with Nutrients: Discover the vital nutrients that enhance brain function and mental clarity. Thriving Under Stress: Learn how to thrive and not just survive in high-pressure situations. Boosting Resilience and Adaptability: Enhance your flexibility and ability to adapt to change. Healing and Growing: Employ time-tested techniques to recover from stress and expand your mental horizons. In a world where the only constant is uncertainty, The Complete Guide to Mental Health: Nutrient Recommendations and Lifestyle Advice equips you with the knowledge and tools to not only weather the storm but to emerge stronger and more focused. Feed your body the nutrients it needs, shift your state of mind with practical strategies, and transform chaos into opportunity. The future may be unpredictable, but your path to wellness doesn't have to be. Empower yourself and your family today with this essential guide to mental health. title: The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma
description: #1 New York Times bestseller “Essential reading for anyone interested in understanding and treating traumatic stress and the scope of its impact on society.” —Alexander McFarlane, Director of the Centre for Traumatic Stress Studies A pioneering researcher transforms our understanding of trauma and offers a bold new paradigm for healing in this New York Times bestseller Trauma is a fact of life. Veterans and their families deal with the painful aftermath of combat; one in five Americans has been molested; one in four grew up with alcoholics; one in three couples have engaged in physical violence. Dr. Bessel van der Kolk, one of the world’s foremost experts on trauma, has spent over three decades working with survivors. In The Body Keeps the Score , he uses recent scientific advances to show how trauma literally reshapes both body and brain, compromising sufferers’ capacities for pleasure, engagement, self-control, and trust. He explores innovative treatments—from neurofeedback and meditation to sports, drama, and yoga—that offer new paths to recovery by activating the brain’s natural neuroplasticity. title: Daddy Issues: A Memoir
description: *INSTANT NATIONAL BESTSELLER* An unflinching memoir from Sofia Franklyn, cocreator of the hit podcast Call Her Daddy , offering an explosive story of power, friendship, reclamation, and surviving yourself. Long before the internet was watching, Sofia Franklyn learned to disappear. Dysfunction was normal and escape was instinct. New York City offered reinvention, and there she met Alex Cooper. They moved quickly: roommates, best friends, business partners. Call Her Daddy became a phenomenon overnight, evolving into a cultural force and transforming its hosts into avatars of a moment and then into targets. But at the height of the show’s early success, their relationship imploded. In hindsight, the warning signs were everywhere. Secrets, omissions, things left unsaid. Millions watched as Sofia went from one half of a beloved duo to the villain in the internet’s messiest breakup. She found herself at rock bottom again, not by the familiar hands of men, but by the unexpected betrayal of another woman. What followed was a private collapse that forced a reckoning, leading Sofia to interrogate her ambition and the cost of being understood as a headline. After years of silence, Sofia tells her side for the first time. Daddy Issues is not a story of revenge. It’s a testimony and a raw, darkly funny portrait of girlhood, friendship, sexuality, agency, and healing. At its core, it is a story of reclamation and the long, brutal work of surviving yourself.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_4"]', '#CardInstanceEmYJe3CXb-AIv_uvSuG_Ag')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_4',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-prim

title: Oh My Gut!: Things You Wish You Knew About Your Gut, Nutrition, and Mental Health.
description: Your everyday guide to the most important and overlooked organ in your body: a clear-eyed journey through the gut, including specially made recipes for Crohn’s, colitis, and IBS. In Oh My Gut! , health and digestion researcher Mili Levran explores the digestive system through an integrative lens of nutrition and the latest tools and tips on the mind-gut connection. Drawing on years of professional experience—as well as her family's personal journey through ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease—Mili answers some of the most important questions that we don’t ask about our most important organ: What role do gut bacteria play in overall health? How does chronic stress affect digestion and inflammation? Why do emotional experiences sometimes manifest as physical symptoms? And what can we do to support the body's natural ability to restore balance? Alongside nineteen of Mili’s own tasty, nutritious, healthy recipes designed to put as little stress on your gut as possible, Oh My Gut! will teach you about: The science of the gut-brain connection and the body's "second brain" The essential role of the microbiome in digestion, immunity, and overall wellness How to use methods from Chinese medicine to balance digestion and whole-body health Practical tools for supporting resilience, reducing inflammation, and improving daily well-being Strategies for developing a healthier relationship with your body and its signals Your gut influences more than just your digestion—it plays a vital role in your immune system, energy levels, mood, mental resilience, and far more. title: The Neuroscience Of Mental Health (2 Books In 1):: Discover The Science Behind Gratitude A
description: Your Anxious Brain Is Not Broken! Is anxiety robbing you of your life? Wearing you out? Always making you feel exhausted even when you're doing nothing? Is your body tensing up without you even noticing? Do you sometimes feel like all you want to do is lie in your bed? All curled up in a ball for the rest of your life? Anxiety is the silent monster of our times. Maybe you suffer from social anxiety, thinking everyone judges you, always, no matter who they are, even your closest friends. Or maybe you overthink situations so much it makes you anxious and you can't find relief… Sometimes you don't even want to get out of bed. But as you're lying there, your heart starts beating really fast and it becomes hard to breathe for no reason... It feels like sleep is the only thing that can bring you peace. You sleep for long hours just to escape the dreadful feeling… yet when you wake up, you're feeling even more tired than before. You just want your life back! And you're not alone! Over 275 million people around the world suffer from anxiety disorders. It might seem like a cruel joke, but anxiety was originally our body's alarm system, meant to keep us safe from the dangers of a harsh world. But in our modern, overstimulated world, this alarm doesn't know when to turn off. So if you want to bring your anxiety under control, you need to understand why your nervous system is stuck in fight-or-flight mode. It's why your brain tends to catastrophize and ruminate constantly. But here's the good news: your brain isn't static! It evolves. And through the power of Neuroplasticity, you have the ability to reshape it and create new, anxiety-free neural pathways. This is not just an empty promise; it's a scientific fact! title: Diagnosis: How We Defeat the Mental Health Epidemic by Labeling Less and Connecting More
description: When rising pro sports executive Eric Kussin’s brain and body shut down, leaving him virtually bedridden for two and a half years, he had no clue how to navigate the convoluted maze that is our modern mental health care system. Diagnosis is Eric’s agonizing story as well as a wakeup call to a society that must be united to help overcome the mental health epidemic. Though awareness and advocacy are greater than ever, personal struggles—from panic episodes and ER visits to suicides and overdoses—have continued to soar. Why such an inverse relationship between awareness and outcomes? From his personal journey, Eric found that we have a system obsessed with the “right” label and trying to fight a “chemical imbalance” with more medications at the expense of getting to the root causes. Alternatively, integrative practitioners helped him unlock the chronic stress and trauma built into his nervous system over three decades, causing physiological and biological changes that ultimately led to his mental health crash. When he rose again, stronger than ever, he became dedicated to reframing the discussion of mental health, creating a worldwide movement energized by the commonality of our emotional pain that we all feel. He discovered that mental health doesn’t afflict, as the commonly cited statistic says, “one in five” people. Rather, all of us—“five in five”—must deal with that shared reality. Hence, #SameHere, the Global Mental Health Movement, was founded. Diagnosis provides tools for better understanding neuroscience and taking preventative action, such as the #SameHere Scale and the STARR “gym for your brain,” before our health declines. title: Mental Health for Men: What Nobody Told You About Strength, Silence, and Why Carrying It A
description: You know something is not right. You are not falling apart visibly. You are showing up, handling it, keeping it moving, being useful, being fine. But underneath the fine, something is grinding. Mental Health for Men is a direct, practical book for men who were taught to push through, stay quiet, keep control, and call that strength. It does not ask readers to perform vulnerability or dress up pain in therapy language. It explains what is happening, why the old strategies stop working, and what a man can actually do next. Inside, readers explore: Why anger is often the only emotion men feel allowed to express, and what may sit underneath it. How depression, anxiety, stress, and shutdown can look different in men. The real cost of silence, performance, work addiction, isolation, and carrying everything alone. How upbringing, shame, pressure, and old survival rules shape adult reactions. What support, therapy, friendship, grief, and repair can look like without turning into a performance. How to build a life that holds, not just a routine that looks impressive. title: The Anxious Generation: How the Great Rewiring of Childhood Is Causing an Epidemic of Ment
description: THE ACCLAIMED #1 NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER with over two million copies sold • A must-read for all parents: the generation-defining investigation into the collapse of youth mental health in the era of smartphones, social media, and big tech—and a plan for a healthier, freer childhood. • A cultural catalyst for the resulting $17.1 Billion Meta Settlement. Named one of the best books of the year by The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times Book Review, The Washington Post, Time, The Economist, New York Post , and Town & Country • One of Barack Obama’s Favorite Books of the Year • Named finalist for the PEN Literary Awards “With tenacity and candor, Haidt lays out the consequences that have come with allowing kids to drift further into the virtual world . . . While also offering suggestions and solutions that could help protect a new generation of kids.” — Time After more than a decade of stability or improvement, the mental health of adolescents plunged in the early 2010s. Rates of depression, anxiety, self-harm, and suicide rose sharply, more than doubling on many measures. Why? In The Anxious Generation , social psychologist Jonathan Haidt (pronounced "height") lays out the facts about the epidemic of teen mental illness that hit many countries at the same time. He then investigates the nature of childhood, including why children need play and independent exploration to mature into competent, thriving adults. Haidt shows how the “play-based childhood” began to decline in the 1980s, and how it was finally wiped out by the arrival of the “phone-based childhood” in the early 2010s.
